name: Archaeological Border complex of Hedeby and the Danevirke
description: Hedeby was a bustling Viking Age trading town at the head of the Schlei inlet in northern Germany, once described by a visiting traveller as a very large city at the end of the world's ocean. Ships and goods crossed a short overland route here between the Baltic and North Seas. Earthen ramparts of the Danevirke still wrap around the buried streets, harbour and graves, and a nearby museum displays the finds.
